newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Iberia calls for flexible night flights.
newsitem.headline: Iberia calls for flexible night flights.

text.p: Iberia has called for more flexible rules concerning night flights at Maastricht Aachen airport.
Iberia's Dutch cargo manager, Ton Jansen, said the recent announcement limiting night flights into Maastricht does restrict the airline's international expansion and express plans.
One of the arguments over night flights has concerned delays to incoming international flights which then are too late to make their scheduled departure before the curfew.
The Madrid-based carrier operates a weekly freighter flight into Maastricht from Buenos Aires and sometimes this flight is subject to delays, Jansen said.

If the delayed flight cannot take-off from the Dutch airport before the night time curfew it then has to stay at the airport until the morning. Also if the crew are then entitled to their rest period further delays and costs are incurred, he said.
"For the time being the inter-continental flight will stay at Maastricht. We do not want the flights to land or depart during the night but sometimes they are delayed," said Jansen.
Last year, Iberia was considering developing an express operation at Maastricht but these plans have been put on hold because of the recent ruling.
"Maastricht offers very good quality handling and a good service but it is diffiicult to expand internationally," he added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 7706
